scenarios.title: A ticket goes through every lane
scenarios.caption: A bug report goes through Triage, Reproduce, Fix, QA and Review, each worked by its own client. None of them moves the ticket: the server does, once it has checked their work.

tickets.title: Orders of exactly $50 still pay shipping

events.caption: triage-bot takes the new ticket and says it belongs to shipping. The server checks that, and moves the ticket to Reproduce.

package.instructions: Name the area that owns the report.

events.caption: repro-bot sends a case: a $50.00 order, which the policy says ships free. The server runs it on the shop's rules, gets $5.99, and moves the ticket to Fix.

package.instructions: Send a subtotal and the shipping the policy says it pays, where the rules charge something else. Close the ticket after two cases that do not reproduce it.

events.caption: fix-bot sends a patch: free shipping from $50.00. The server runs the repro case and four cases from earlier fixes on it. All pass, so the ticket goes to QA.

package.instructions: Send a patch to the free-shipping threshold. The server runs the repro case and the cases earlier fixes were checked against on it.

check.message: free from $50.00: the repro case and 4 cases from earlier fixes pass

events.caption: qa-bot has the server try $49.99, $50.00 and $50.01 on the patched rules. All three charge what the policy says, so the ticket goes to Review.

package.instructions: Send subtotals to run on the patched rules, around the threshold.

check.message: 3 of 3 pass on the patched rules; sent to Review

events.caption: Sam, the one person on the board, approves the fix, and the server marks the ticket done.

package.instructions: Approve the fix, or send it back with a reason.

scenarios.title: An agent tries to skip ahead
scenarios.caption: fix-bot asks for the ticket before it reaches Fix, then tries to approve its own fix. The server refuses both, and the ticket carries on as normal.

tickets.title: Orders of exactly $40 still pay shipping

events.caption: triage-bot files the ticket under shipping, and the server moves it to Reproduce.

package.instructions: Name the area that owns the report.

events.caption: fix-bot asks for the ticket before anyone has reproduced the bug. The ticket is not in Fix, so the server has nothing to give it.

problem.message: T-13 is in Reproducing, not in fix

events.caption: repro-bot shows the bug: a $40.00 order pays $3.99, and the policy says it ships free. The ticket moves to Fix.

package.instructions: Send a subtotal and the shipping the policy says it pays, where the rules charge something else. Close the ticket after two cases that do not reproduce it.

events.caption: Now fix-bot can claim it. Its patch passes the repro case and the cases from earlier fixes, and the ticket goes to QA.

package.instructions: Send a patch to the free-shipping threshold. The server runs the repro case and the cases earlier fixes were checked against on it.

check.message: free from $40.00: the repro case and 3 cases from earlier fixes pass

events.caption: qa-bot's three orders around $40 all charge what the policy says. The ticket goes to Review.

package.instructions: Send subtotals to run on the patched rules, around the threshold.

check.message: 3 of 3 pass on the patched rules; sent to Review

events.caption: fix-bot tries to approve its own fix. Only a reviewer may send Approve, so the server refuses it, and the ticket stays in Review.
Sam approves the fix, and the server marks the ticket done.

package.instructions: Approve the fix, or send it back with a reason.

scenarios.title: A fix that breaks an earlier case
scenarios.caption: fix-bot's first patch has a typo. It fixes the reported order but breaks a case an earlier fix was checked against, so the server rejects it.

tickets.title: Free shipping starts at $75, the policy says $60

events.caption: triage-bot files the ticket under shipping, and the server moves it to Reproduce.

package.instructions: Name the area that owns the report.

events.caption: repro-bot shows the bug: a $60.00 order pays $4.99, and the policy says it ships free. The ticket moves to Fix.

package.instructions: Send a subtotal and the shipping the policy says it pays, where the rules charge something else. Close the ticket after two cases that do not reproduce it.

events.caption: fix-bot sends free from $6.00, a typo for $60. The $60.00 order passes, but an earlier fix's $20.00 case would now ship free. The server rejects the patch.

package.instructions: Send a patch to the free-shipping threshold. The server runs the repro case and the cases earlier fixes were checked against on it.

check.message: $20.00 pays $0.00 with this patch; the policy says $4.99

ticket.note: patch refused: $20.00 pays $0.00 with this patch; the policy says $4.99

events.caption: fix-bot sends free from $60.00. The repro case and all three earlier cases pass, and the ticket goes to QA.

check.message: free from $60.00: the repro case and 3 cases from earlier fixes pass

events.caption: qa-bot's three orders around $60 all charge what the policy says. The ticket goes to Review.

package.instructions: Send subtotals to run on the patched rules, around the threshold.

check.message: 3 of 3 pass on the patched rules; sent to Review

events.caption: Sam approves the fix, and the server marks the ticket done.

package.instructions: Approve the fix, or send it back with a reason.

scenarios.title: QA finds what the fix missed
scenarios.caption: fix-bot's patch passes every case the server has. qa-bot tries orders around the threshold, finds one the patch gets wrong, and the ticket goes back to Fix.

events.caption: triage-bot files the ticket under shipping, and the server moves it to Reproduce.

package.instructions: Name the area that owns the report.

events.caption: repro-bot shows the bug: a $100.00 order pays $7.50, and the policy says it ships free. The ticket moves to Fix.

package.instructions: Send a subtotal and the shipping the policy says it pays, where the rules charge something else. Close the ticket after two cases that do not reproduce it.

events.caption: fix-bot sends free above $99.00. That gets $100.00 right, and the cases from earlier fixes pass too, so the server sends the ticket to QA.

package.instructions: Send a patch to the free-shipping threshold. The server runs the repro case and the cases earlier fixes were checked against on it.

check.message: free above $99.00: the repro case and 3 cases from earlier fixes pass

events.caption: qa-bot tries $99.50. The patch ships it free, but the policy charges $7.50 below $100. QA did its job, and the server sends the ticket back to Fix.

package.instructions: Send subtotals to run on the patched rules, around the threshold.

check.message: $99.50 pays $0.00 on the patched rules; the policy says $7.50; sent back to Fix

events.caption: fix-bot claims the ticket again and sends free from $100.00. Every case passes, and the ticket goes back to QA.

package.instructions: Send a patch to the free-shipping threshold. The server runs the repro case and the cases earlier fixes were checked against on it.

check.message: free from $100.00: the repro case and 3 cases from earlier fixes pass

events.caption: This time all three of qa-bot's orders charge what the policy says. The ticket goes to Review.

package.instructions: Send subtotals to run on the patched rules, around the threshold.

check.message: 3 of 3 pass on the patched rules; sent to Review

events.caption: Sam approves the fix, and the server marks the ticket done.

scenarios.title: A bug that does not reproduce
scenarios.caption: The shop's rules already match the policy. repro-bot may close the ticket, but only once the server has run two of its cases and neither showed the bug.

events.caption: triage-bot files the ticket under shipping, and the server moves it to Reproduce.

package.instructions: Name the area that owns the report.

events.caption: repro-bot tries the reported order, $75.00. The rules ship it free, as the policy says. The bug does not reproduce, and the ticket stays in Reproduce.

package.instructions: Send a subtotal and the shipping the policy says it pays, where the rules charge something else. Close the ticket after two cases that do not reproduce it.

check.message: $75.00 pays $0.00, which matches the policy: not reproduced

events.caption: repro-bot asks to close the ticket. The server refuses: a close needs two cases that did not reproduce, and it has run one.

problem.message: Close needs at least two cases the server ran that did not reproduce it.

events.caption: repro-bot tries the edge of the policy, $50.00. It ships free too, as it should. That is two cases.

check.message: $50.00 pays $0.00, which matches the policy: not reproduced

events.caption: repro-bot asks again. The server counts two cases it ran itself, closes the ticket, and moves it to Done.

ticket.note: cannot reproduce: 2 cases matched the policy
